chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Hammam, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah, that al-Abbas narrated to him, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Ali ibn Maymun al-Saqqaf, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Ali, it has reached me that some people from our Shia pass by one year, two years, or more than that, without visiting al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him).'

I said, 'May I be your ransom, I know many people with this description.' He said, 'By Allah, they have missed their due portion, turned away from the reward of Allah, and distanced themselves from the proximity of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) in Paradise.'
I said, 'If a man sends someone else on his behalf, does that suffice for him?' He said, 'Yes, and his going himself is greater in reward and better for him with his Lord.'

key_terms.أَخْرَجَ عَنْهُ: sent a representative on behalf of someone
key_terms.السَّنَةُ وَالسَّنَتَانِ: one or two years (period of neglect)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and reward for visiting Imam al-Husayn's shrine if one cannot go personally?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) addresses the spiritual consequence of prolonged neglect in visiting the shrine of Imam al-Husayn (peace be upon him), warning that such delay causes believers to miss their designated spiritual portion (*hazz*) and distance themselves from the Prophet’s proximity in Paradise. He clarifies the jurisprudential ruling that sending a representative (*mu'tamad*) is sufficient to fulfill the obligation, yet emphasizes that personal pilgrimage remains superior in reward and merit. This highlights the Shia emphasis on *Ziyarat* as both a communal duty and a deeply personal act of devotion that strengthens the bond with the Ahl al-Bayt.
